expert_three.re_ground_pass: RAN (conditionally, on ungrounded findings) and demonstrably fired: 9 findings reground_confirmed with reground_seat set. See stages[5] (index for re-ground) / grounding validation stage.
expert_three.cross_family_confirmation: RAN (conditionally, on single-family blocking findings post-B1) and demonstrably fired: 62 findings carry cross_family, incl. 29 confirmed and 5 unresolved; a further 25 refutations proceeded into dispute+Tech Lead (cross_family='tech_lead_sustained').
expert_three.grounding_demotion: THERE IS NO GROUNDING DEMOTION STAGE. No stage in run_review demotes a severity or removes a finding merely because grounding failed. Precisely: (1) initial grounding failure only MARKS the finding grounding='ungrounded' and queues it for re-ground (core.py:4121-4135) — severity and gate eligibility unchanged at that point; (2) in re-ground, a finding leaves the gate list ONLY if a seat itself answers 'withdrawn' in _reground_call (core.py:1075-1097, applied core.py:4293-4301) — a model withdrawal with a stated reason, preserved in the full report's withdrawn_findings (a list to_attempt_record drops, so any withdrawals in attempt 1 are uncountable from attempt-1.jsonl); a 'confirmed' answer with a quote validating against the region restores it as grounding='reground_confirmed' with the new quote; (3) if re-ground is UNRESOLVED, the finding STAYS in merged at its original severity and still blocks if blocking-severity — grounding failure does not demote it — and separately, if the computed gate would otherwise be PASS, unresolved grounding flips it to INCONCLUSIVE with a 'human must decide' reason (core.py:4882-4889 reasons; :4998-5013 flip). In attempt 1 that flip never fired: 0 findings with grounding='unresolved' in the persisted records and 0 inconclusive gates. The only severity demotion in the path is Policy B1 (_apply_gate_profile), which is lens-attribution-based (solely-operations, uncorroborated), NOT grounding-based.

seat_prompts: The bench path uses the PRODUCT'S OWN prompt construction, not bench-specific prompts. run_review builds every seat prompt from core's _REVIEW_PROMPT (core.py prompt construction in job building, :3981-3986, formatted with LENSES[lens], the caller context, test summary and the batch), the re-ground prompt from core's _REGROUND_PROMPT via _reground_call, the cross-family prompt from core's _XCONFIRM_PROMPT via _xconfirm_call, and the Tech Lead prompt inside core's _tech_lead_call. Bench-specific elements are only: (a) the GenerationSeat transport wrapper (record/replay cache, retry budgets, shadow cost) that run_review calls as an ordinary provider callable, (b) transports/params from bench/scripts/run_generation_v2.py build_transport/PARAMS, and (c) the per-case context string ('[bench-case: id] + title + case context'). file_context and agents_context were NOT passed, so no _FILE_CONTEXT_HEADER/_AGENTS_CONTEXT_HEADER suffix was appended — prompts were the pre-D1/pre-L1 byte construction core's docstring says bench/registered runs rely on.
bottom_line: Not raw panel + B1 alone, and not the full product gate either: attempt 1 measured the full in-core adjudication pipeline that needs no external inputs — deterministic scan, product seat calls/repair, grounding validation + re-ground (§2b), coverage, merge, line basis, Policy B1 (_apply_gate_profile), platform-scope labelling, cross-family confirmation (§2c), dispute adequacy grading and binding Tech Lead adjudication — all demonstrably exercised in the records (54 B1 demotions, 9 re-ground confirmations, 62 cross_family labels, 25 disputes all Tech-Lead-sustained) — while every stage that needs a caller-supplied input was absent because the confirmation chain passes none of them: project policy (.codereview.toml, Epic B) and with it risk/tiering/diversity (Epics E1-E4), the Epic C evidence rule, precedents (§2e), fixture scope, a designated tech_lead, probe_fn, tech-lead shadow, file_context (D1), agents_context (L1), test_results, waivers and notifications.
not_measured: Project policy file evaluation (Epic B): policy=None — no .codereview.toml rules applied, no policy violations (blocking or advisory), no policy-sourced gate profile, no waivers honoured (waivers also not passed).
Epic C evidence rule: evidence=None — no evidence runner record was collected or judged; required-evidence failed/missing -> BLOCKED and unavailable -> INCONCLUSIVE consequences were never evaluated.

Precedents (§2e): precedents=None — no standing-finding classification against a precedent store, no attach_function_keys/apply_precedents, no precedent candidates persisted (precedent_eligible marks on 12 findings are inert without a store).
Fixture scope classification: fixture_scope=None — no manifest-declared fixture findings were separated; any fixture-shaped content in a case diff was judged as product code.

Designated Tech Lead: tech_lead=None — adjudication used core's auto-selection of an independent served seat (all 25 by deepseek); a user-designated seat, its rejection/substitution path, and tech_lead_timeout override were not measured.

Builder-probe channel: probe_fn=None — no probe round was (or could be) run; a needs_probe Tech Lead decision would have escalated instead of probing (all 25 actual decisions were sustain_finding with probe_rounds=0, so the gap did not bite in this attempt).

Tech Lead shadow adjudication: tech_lead_shadow=False (default) — shadow_adjudicate never ran (the dispute-embedded reason_check/trace_gate_shadow shadow evaluations did run; they are a different, unconditional mechanism).

file_context (acceptance D1): not passed — reviewers judged the diff alone, with no post-change file contents attached; this is precisely the diff-only configuration whose false 'undefined symbol' risk D1 was built to mitigate in real product runs.
agents_context (Epic L1): not passed — no AGENTS.md guidance (incl. any '## Code Review Rules') was ingested into prompts.

Risk score / tiered panels / escalation (Epics E1/E2/E4) and panel diversity (Epic E3): all policy-gated, policy=None — the run was always the single-stage full panel; reduced-panel, escalation-trigger and builder-family-exclusion behaviour were not measured.
Test results: test_results not passed ([]) — deterministic_scan's test-failure blocker and the prompt's test-results section reflect 'no test commands were run' for every case.
Lens pinning via lens_seats, record_extra, private attestation, progress/notify (Epic L4): none passed (lens_seats is in any case superseded by the explicit seat_lenses binding).

Fallback serving as an outcome: the correctness->openai fallback was declared and wired, but no banked record was fallback-served, so fallback-served gate behaviour is unmeasured by the scored records (generation-phase unscored/content-failed jobs are a separate, generation-record matter).
